home.title: Home
home.location_banner_subtitle: Enable location access to unlock your personalised air quality dashboard and health insights.
home.pick_birthday_subtitle: Pregnancy cycle is over and now you can pick birth date
home.week_desc_w01: Fertilization happens, and the tiny ball of cells travels to the uterus and implants into the lining.
home.week_desc_w02: Fertilization happens, and the tiny ball of cells travels to the uterus and implants into the lining.
home.week_desc_w03: The neural plate begins to form, which will become your baby’s brain and spinal cord.
home.week_desc_w04: The neural tube closes, the heart starts to form and beat, and small limb buds appear.
home.week_desc_w05: The heart develops chambers, the face begins forming, and the first signs of arms and legs show.
home.week_desc_w06: Arms lengthen, ears and eyes start shaping, and the heart is beating strongly.
home.week_desc_w07: The face becomes more defined, the palate starts forming, and fingers begin to separate.
home.week_desc_w08: Major organs finish their basic formation, the palate rises, and the ears continue to develop.
home.week_desc_w09: Your baby enters the foetal stage — the head grows quickly, and the liver begins making blood cells.
home.week_desc_w10: Kidneys begin working, the palate fuses, facial features refine, and external genitals start differentiating.
home.week_desc_w11: The palate closes fully, the brain develops rapidly, and the baby’s body lengthens.
home.week_desc_w12: Organs are formed, the face looks more human, and movements begin though you can’t feel them yet.
home.week_desc_w13: Bones harden, teeth buds form, and the placenta is now nourishing your baby effectively.
home.week_desc_w14: Muscles and nerves coordinate, your baby can make facial expressions, and the thyroid begins to work.
home.week_desc_w15: Bones continue to grow, the baby can move arms and legs, and taste buds develop.
home.week_desc_w16: The eyes and ears are well formed, the nervous system develops, and you may soon feel movement.
home.week_desc_w17: Fat begins to store under the skin, the skeleton hardens, and the baby moves more vigorously.
home.week_desc_w18: The lungs branch, the skin is covered in vernix, and movements become stronger and more noticeable.
home.week_desc_w19: Fine hair (lanugo) covers the body, senses develop, and the baby practices swallowing.
home.week_desc_w20: Halfway through pregnancy — the baby measures about 25 cm, movements are clear, and organs mature further.
home.week_desc_w21: Surfactant starts forming in the lungs, the brain grows quickly, and the baby hears your heartbeat.
home.week_desc_w22: The baby reacts to sounds, hair becomes visible, and movements are well coordinated.
home.week_desc_w23: The baby is stronger, skin less transparent, lungs continue developing, and hearing is active.
home.week_desc_w24: The baby is now considered viable with intensive care, lungs develop sacs, and the brain organizes sleep cycles.
home.week_desc_w25: The brain forms grooves, taste buds are active, and movements become more coordinated.
home.week_desc_w26: The eyes open, the baby responds to sounds, lungs and brain mature further, and fat accumulates.
home.week_desc_w27: Entering the third trimester — the brain grows rapidly, the lungs develop, and sleep–wake cycles are regular.
home.week_desc_w28: The baby weighs about 1.1 kg, immune protection from mother increases, and the eyes respond to light.
home.week_desc_w29: The brain develops folds, fat deposits under the skin, and the baby’s kicks are strong and regular.
home.week_desc_w30: The brain connections multiply, the baby practices breathing, and weight gain accelerates.
home.week_desc_w31: The nervous system matures, the lungs expand, rhythmic breathing begins, and the baby gains strength.
home.week_desc_w32: The baby weighs around 1.7 kg, bones harden, the skin smooths, and the brain grows quickly.
home.week_desc_w33: The baby nears 2 kg, the immune system strengthens, the brain’s white matter develops, and movements are complex.
home.week_desc_w34: The baby weighs over 2 kg, fat accumulates, the lungs nearly mature, and the brain is very active.
home.week_desc_w35: The lungs are almost fully developed, the baby continues to gain weight, and the body prepares for life outside.
home.week_desc_w36: The baby weighs about 2.6 kg, organs are ready, fat stores build, and the head likely engages in the pelvis.
home.week_desc_w37: Considered early term — the baby weighs ~2.9 kg, organs are mature, and the placenta begins to age.
home.week_desc_w38: Full term — the baby weighs ~3.1 kg, continues to gain fat, and is ready for birth.
home.week_desc_w39: The baby weighs ~3.3 kg, brain and fat growth peak, and the body prepares naturally for labour.
home.week_desc_w40: The baby weighs ~3.4–3.5 kg, all systems are mature, the placenta begins to decline, and birth is imminent.

mary_hydration_300.title: Drink 300 ml of water now
mary_hydration_300.purpose: Have another 300 ml before noon, and add a vitamin-C fruit such as an orange with your next meal.

mary_shift_midday_work.title: Move demanding tasks away from midday
mary_shift_midday_work.purpose: Aim for 09:00–11:00 or 16:00–18:00 and avoid the hottest, busiest 12:30–14:30 window when you can.

mary_shaded_rest.title: Take a 10-minute seated rest in shade
mary_shaded_rest.purpose: Cool down around 13:00 and again near 17:00; a damp cloth can help you feel more comfortable.

wellbeing_clean_air_breathing.title: Take one quiet minute in clean air
wellbeing_clean_air_breathing.purpose: Try slow, rhythmic abdominal breathing in a smoke-free indoor space.

wellbeing_gentle_wind_down.title: Make tonight’s wind-down gentler
wellbeing_gentle_wind_down.purpose: Choose a screen-free routine and give yourself a quiet space to decompress before sleep.

wellbeing_cool_pause.title: Cool down and pause when stress rises
wellbeing_cool_pause.purpose: Move to a cooler shaded space, sip water and place a damp cloth on your neck or forehead.

diet_vitamin_c_pairing.title: Pair an iron-rich food with vitamin C
diet_vitamin_c_pairing.purpose: Add a locally available fruit or vegetable rich in vitamin C alongside an iron-rich meal.

behaviour_cleaner_cooking_window.title: Create a cleaner cooking space
behaviour_cleaner_cooking_window.purpose: Cook outdoors or under an open-sided shelter when possible, and fully extinguish coals after cooking.

activity_shaded_route.title: Choose the shaded, lower-traffic route
activity_shaded_route.purpose: Prefer a short route with shade and fewer dusty or congested roads.

behaviour_ventilate_when_air_clears.title: Refresh indoor air at a cleaner time
behaviour_ventilate_when_air_clears.purpose: When outdoor air feels clearer, open opposite windows or doors briefly to improve airflow.

activity_gentle_mobility_pause.title: Take a gentle mobility pause
activity_gentle_mobility_pause.purpose: Relax your shoulders and ankles with slow, comfortable movements, then sit if you need to.

wellbeing_grounding_senses.title: Try a one-minute grounding pause
wellbeing_grounding_senses.purpose: Notice what you can see, hear and feel around you, without judging how the moment is going.
